ops.title: ccx vcs ship rebase autostash is not always reapplied, silently dropping foreign uncommitted work
ops.premise:
On the jj/git lane, `ccx vcs ship [paths...]` fetches and rebases the stack onto the
target before committing, autostashing uncommitted work that falls outside the scoped
paths. The documented contract is that this work is restored afterward, leaving a
concurrent session's changes untouched.

In at least one run it was not. In /Users/yasyf/Code/fusekit a ship autostashed three
foreign modified files under holder/ and never reapplied them: the working copy came
back clean, `refs/stash` was empty, and the changes survived only as a dangling
"On main: autostash" commit (7c3b5d4). A ship in a sibling repo minutes earlier
(cc-pool, same session, same fetch+rebase path) reapplied its autostash correctly.

Falsifiable premise: the autostash reapply is conditionally skipped or silently
swallowed rather than unconditionally performed -- e.g. on a path-scoped commit, when
the apply conflicts, or when the rebase takes a fast-forward branch -- and the failure
leaves no `refs/stash` entry, so the only recovery is a dangling-commit hunt via
reflog/fsck. If true, any ship run in a shared working copy can silently destroy a
concurrent session's uncommitted work with no error and no stash ref.

ops.text: fusekit: 3 modified files (holder/broker_process.go, holder/broker_process_test.go, holder/runtime.go) were autostashed by ship's fetch+rebase and vanished from the working copy. Recovered from dangling commit 7c3b5d4 with 'git diff fd839e2 7c3b5d4 -- holder/ | git apply'; verified byte-identical (git diff 7c3b5d4 -- holder/ empty). Pinned as tag rescue/fusekit-autostash in that repo, plus a patch at ~/.claude/rescue/fusekit-holder-1786911462.patch.
cc-pool hit the same fetch+rebase in the same session and its autostash WAS reapplied correctly -- nothing lost. So the failure is intermittent/conditional, not systematic.
After the loss there was no refs/stash entry. Whatever created the autostash left no stash ref to recover from, which is why the working copy looked legitimately clean.

A later scoped ship in the SAME repo (fusekit, paths go.mod + CHANGELOG.md) rebased over an advanced origin with the restored holder/ work plus new foreign catalogworker/ files present, and did NOT drop anything -- holder/ diff sha256 c9766d4a6332eea900b6f0475b48c7e8fbdd66309b24e8f5e679e1ad4e12ffe4 stable across the ship. So 'path-scoped ship + foreign work + rebase' alone does not reproduce it; some further condition is required.
